display.title: Sefiras HaOmer at Home, Part 2: Rabbi Akiva, Lag BaOmer and Matan Torah
display.summary_short: A father in Yiddish tells his young son about Rabbi Akiva's students, Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Lag BaOmer, the days of Sefirah and the giving of the Torah at Har Sinai.
display.summary_long: The second Yiddish home recording of a father with his son, about to turn three, during Sefiras HaOmer. First he tells of Rabbi Akiva and his twenty-four thousand students, who were punished because they lacked Ahavas Yisroel until Lag BaOmer, and they sing 'V'ahavta l'reacha kamocha', Rabbi Akiva's great rule of the Torah. Next comes Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who hid from the Romans in a cave with his son for twelve years, living on a carob tree and a spring of water and learning Torah; he passed away on Lag BaOmer, which is why children go out with bows and arrows. The father then describes the Jews' journey from Mitzrayim, growing better each day by listening to the yetzer tov and not the yetzer hara, until they reach Har Sinai on Rosh Chodesh Sivan. He paints Matan Torah: fire, smoke, thunder, the shofar, and Hashem's first word, Anochi, while the whole world falls silent. He explains why we eat dairy on Shavuos, plays the niggun Atah Hareisa, and the recording ends with 'We Want Moshiach Now'.
display.lesson: Love every Jew, listen to the yetzer tov, and prepare each day of Sefirah to receive the Torah.
